title: FromBody
description: Learn how to bind request body data.

data.text: **[FromBody]** tells ASP.NET Core to read the entire request body and deserialize it into a .NET object. It is the standard way to accept JSON payloads for POST and PUT operations.

When you apply [FromBody] to an action parameter, the framework uses the registered input formatter — typically System.Text.Json — to read the raw request stream and materialize it into your DTO or entity type.

terms.definition: An attribute that instructs model binding to read the parameter value from the HTTP request body.
A service that reads the request body and converts it to a .NET type. ASP.NET Core includes System.Text.Json and supports third-party formatters.
The process of converting JSON text into .NET objects using an input formatter.
The HTTP header that indicates the media type of the request body, such as application/json.

data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant M as Middleware
    participant B as Model Binder
    participant A as Action
    C->>M: POST /api/users (JSON body)
    M->>B: Read request body stream
    B->>B: Deserialize JSON to DTO
    B->>A: Inject bound parameter
    A->>C: 201 Created with location header

data.text: Apply [FromBody] to complex types that represent a create or update payload. Use data annotations on the DTO to enforce validation before the action body executes.

data.title: FromBody with Validation
data.content: A POST action that binds a JSON body to a validated DTO.

data.title: ApiController Makes Validation Automatic
data.text: When a controller is decorated with [ApiController], invalid [FromBody] payloads automatically return 400 Bad Request with RFC 7807 ProblemDetails. You rarely need to check ModelState manually.

cards.title: [FromBody] Attribute
cards.description: Explicitly binds a single parameter from the request body using input formatters.
pros: Works with JSON, XML, and custom formatters
cons: Only one parameter per action by default

cards.title: [FromForm] Attribute
cards.description: Binds from form data, typically used in MVC views or file uploads.

cards.title: [ApiController] Auto-Binding
cards.description: In API controllers, complex parameters are inferred as [FromBody] without the attribute.
cons: Still limited to one complex parameter

items.text: Use a dedicated request DTO instead of binding entities directly
Return 400 with ValidationProblem when ModelState is invalid
Use CreatedAtAction on success to return the new resource location
Accept only the media types your API supports
Never trust the client — validate again on the server even if [ApiController] helps

data.title: Implement a POST Endpoint
data.description: Create a POST endpoint that accepts a JSON body, validates it, and returns the created resource.
steps: Define a CreateProductRequest DTO with Name, SKU, Price, and ReleaseDate properties.
Add validation attributes: [Required] and [StringLength] for Name, [Range] for Price, and a custom [RegularExpression] for SKU.
Create a POST api/products action that accepts [FromBody] CreateUserRequest.
Return ValidationProblem(ModelState) when the payload is invalid.
Return CreatedAtAction with the new product when valid.
data.expectedOutcome: A POST endpoint that rejects malformed JSON with 400 and returns 201 Created with a Location header for valid requests.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: [FromBody] binds JSON or other formatted payloads from the request stream
Use DTOs with validation attributes for create and update actions
[ApiController] returns automatic 400 responses for invalid bodies
Avoid binding entities directly; prefer request DTOs
data.takeaway: FromBody turns JSON into usable .NET objects with built-in validation.
